decision: Jeremy, 2026-10-10: freeze measured values; no annual re-derivation job. 2-QB measured separately, not extrapolated.
method: Position share of listed players x 15 rounds = rostered per team; minus starters (1 QB / 2 RB / 2 WR / 1 TE / FLEX split RB/WR / K / DEF; 2-QB format: 2 QB); divided by starters. Human picks in FFC 12-team PPR 15-round drafts with K and DEF. Tables listing fewer than 12 x 15 x 0.9 players are rejected as truncated (one_qb 2022 excluded).
convention_use: Roster convention rule 1 picks two_qb when the roster has 2 QB slots or a superflex slot, else one_qb. FFC labels the format '2 QB' and does not separate superflex; use it for both until superflex-specific data exists.
reproduce: python3 pipelines/derive_market_bench.py --derive (reads data/inputs/market_bench/ffc_adp_<format>_<year>.json). Re-derived values differ from the frozen ones by at most 0.02 (one_qb QB 0.87 vs 0.88, K 0.02 vs 0.00: the original K/DEF and skill-only draft sets were measured on slightly different tables); the frozen values are authoritative.

two_qb.note: A 12-team 2-QB league rosters about 31 QBs of 32 NFL starters, so QB backups are supply-capped; scaling the 1-QB ratio would predict 1.76 backup QBs per team against 0.56 observed.
